A type has value semantics when a variable holds its value outright: copying it produces a second, independent value, changing one never changes the other, and

The problem is code that expects an independent value and gets a reference to shared state instead. A reference into a container follows the object it names, so if an operation on the container moves elements around while you still hold that reference, it ends up naming a different element, and every access still looks legal, because the object at that address is alive. Taking a value, a copy, before anything changes removes this failure instead of chasing each place it can appear.
